title: A High-Quality Workflow for Multi-Resolution Scientific Data Reduction and Visualization
problem: Multi-resolution methods like AMR enhance storage efficiency but cannot be universally deployed, and integrating lossy compression with multi-resolution techniques faces significant barriers preventing their joint optimization.
motivation: HPC applications generate vast data volumes requiring efficient storage and compression strategies to make scientific simulations practical and cost-effective.
method: The workflow employs a compression-oriented Region of Interest extraction method to transform uniform data into multi-resolution format. It optimizes three distinct compressors for optimal performance on multi-resolution data. Finally, it incorporates advanced uncertainty visualization to assess the quality impact of lossy compression.
key_novelty: A compression-oriented ROI extraction method that transforms uniform simulations into multi-resolution format, extending multi-resolution compression techniques beyond native AMR applications.
contributions: Compression-oriented ROI extraction for converting uniform data to multi-resolution representation
Optimization of three distinct compressors for multi-resolution data, achieving up to 3.3x compression ratio improvement
Advanced uncertainty visualization method for assessing lossy compression quality impacts
End-to-end workflow supporting both uniform and AMR simulation compression

metrics.accuracy: data quality loss under fixed compression ratio
metrics.other: compression ratio improvement (up to 3.3x vs SOTA)

baselines: SOTA multi-resolution and lossy compression methods
limitations: Specific limitations of the workflow beyond applicability constraints are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Multi-resolution lossy compression for HPC data reduction
